llms.summary: KORUM is a technology platform for schools (through their parents’ association or owner), grassroots sports clubs and cultural organisations. It combines an ideas box with a quorum, all-or-nothing crowdfunding campaigns, QR ticketing and raffles, friendly local businesses and Mi Hucha.
llms.money: Payments, the holding of funds and refunds are executed by PAYCOMET, a payment institution authorised by the Bank of Spain. KORUM is not a financial institution and does not hold funds. If an initiative does not reach its goal, 100% is refunded to each person, to the original payment method. KORUM never intermediates or charges commissions to suppliers of works or equipment: the organisation chooses freely.
figures: The first {exempt} of each school year pays no commission; after that, {t1Rate}, {t2Rate} or {t3Rate} depending on the size of the initiative (bands up to {t1Max} and {t2Max}).
Payment gateway: {gatewayRate} plus {gatewayFixed} per contribution, included in the goal families see.
Tickets and raffle tickets: “digital management fees” of {ticketFixed} plus {ticketRate} of the price.
Business sponsorship: 100% of the chosen level reaches the initiative; the advertising management fee ({sponsorFee} plus VAT) is added on top.

pricing.title: Current rates
pricing.caption: KORUM rates
pricing.noteFlat: The net amount is what the organisation needs to pay for the improvement. The rate is decided by the initiative’s total net amount and applies only to the part above the exempt amount.
pricing.noteMarginal: The net amount is what the organisation needs to pay for the improvement. Each band pays only on the part of the net amount that falls inside it.
pricing.tier1Value: {t1Rate} on the part above the exempt amount
pricing.tier2Value: {t2Rate} on the part above the exempt amount
pricing.tier3Value: {t3Rate} on the part above the exempt amount
pricing.maintOn: {maintFee} per campaign, up to a yearly cap of {maintCap}
pricing.gatewayValue: {gatewayRate} plus {gatewayFixed} per contribution, included in the goal families see
pricing.ticketsValue: “Digital management fees”: {ticketFixed} plus {ticketRate} of the price, always itemised before paying
pricing.sponsorsValue: 100% of the chosen level reaches the initiative. The advertising management fee ({sponsorFee} plus VAT) is added on top and paid by the business
pricing.voluntaryValue: Optional and unticked by default; you choose the amount from zero. It changes nothing about your donation
pricing.disclaimer: The final goal of each initiative is calculated by the organisation’s Studio with its real quote; the simulator on the home page gives an estimate.

colegios.title: Fundraising for schools and parents’ groups
colegios.description: Fund climate control, shade or digital whiteboards with all-or-nothing campaigns, double signatures and a 100% refund if the goal is not reached.
colegios.h1: How to fund improvements at your school without handling cash
colegios.answer: KORUM lets a school or its parents’ association propose an improvement, approve it with a double signature and fund it with families’ contributions in an all-or-nothing campaign: if the goal is not reached, 100% is refunded to each person. The first {exempt} of each school year pays no commission.

sections.title: What your school can do
bullets: Open an ideas box with a quorum so families can propose and back improvements.
Launch all-or-nothing campaigns for climate control, playground shade, digital whiteboards or the end-of-year trip.
Sell tickets and raffle tickets with QR codes at festivals and parties, with capacity control.
Set class challenges (from the first year of nursery to the last year of compulsory secondary school) and celebrate what is achieved.
Export Model 182 in one click if the organisation falls under Law 49/2002.

sections.title: Who signs and who gets paid
paragraphs: A state school always takes part through its parents’ association, which is the organisation that owns the funds. Subsidised and private schools register through their owner.

Approving an idea and releasing funds requires the signatures of two different people: the head of the school and the chair of the parents’ association. Money is collected through Paycomet, held until the goal is reached, and paid to the organisation or directly to its supplier with the invoice in hand.

sections.title: Complete freedom to choose your supplier
paragraphs: KORUM never intermediates or approves suppliers of works or equipment, and never charges them commissions. Your organisation enters the quote from the supplier it prefers and the platform works out the goal.

sections.title: Class challenges, always positive
paragraphs: Classes add participating families to unlock a shared prize. What is achieved is celebrated (“Class 3B already has 28 families”); nobody is singled out and amounts are never compared between classes.

sections.title: What it costs
paragraphs: Registering the school is free. The first {exempt} of each school year pays no commission; after that, the commission runs from {t1Rate} to {t3Rate} depending on the size of the initiative. All rates are on the pricing page.

colegios.ctaTitle: Start with your school’s ideas box
colegios.ctaText: Registration is free and takes a few minutes. No cash, and a 100% refund if the goal is not reached.

clubes.title: Fundraising for sports clubs
clubes.description: Fund kit, travel or facilities with all-or-nothing campaigns, QR tickets and raffles, and a 100% refund if the goal is not reached.
clubes.h1: How to raise funds for a grassroots sports club
clubes.answer: KORUM gives a grassroots sports club an orderly way to raise money: all-or-nothing campaigns for kit, travel or facilities, QR tickets and raffles for its events, and positive team challenges. If a campaign does not reach its goal, 100% is refunded. The first {exempt} of each season pays no commission.

sections.title: Built for how a club works
bullets: Teams by category (from the youngest age groups to seniors) plus supporters and former players.
Double signature between the club’s main manager and its treasurer or chair.
Campaigns for kit, equipment, travel or facility improvements.
Model 182 in one click if the organisation falls under Law 49/2002.

sections.title: Tickets, raffles and the door
paragraphs: Sell tickets with controlled capacity and numbered raffle tickets. Volunteers check people in at the door with their phone camera, using an event PIN and installing nothing. The raffle draw is held on screen and leaves a record.
Raffles and lotteries are regulated by each autonomous community and may require prior notification or authorisation: the organisation confirms it complies with its own rules before publishing.

sections.title: Team challenges, no pressure
paragraphs: Each team adds families to unlock a shared prize. Challenges are always shown in a positive way and every club can switch them off.

sections.title: Supplier independence
paragraphs: KORUM never intermediates suppliers or charges them commissions: the club freely chooses whom it buys from and budgets with.

sections.title: What it costs
paragraphs: Registration is free and the first {exempt} of each season pays no commission. Tickets and raffle tickets carry “digital management fees” of {ticketFixed} plus {ticketRate} of the price, always itemised before paying.

clubes.ctaTitle: Register your club in a few minutes
clubes.ctaText: Open campaigns, sell tickets with QR codes and celebrate every goal with your supporters.

culturales.title: Funding cultural organisation projects
culturales.description: Bands, choirs, theatres and associations: fund projects with all-or-nothing campaigns, QR tickets and a 100% refund if the goal is not reached.
culturales.h1: How to fund the projects of a cultural organisation
culturales.answer: KORUM helps an association, band, choir, school or theatre group fund instruments, costumes, tours or activities with all-or-nothing campaigns: the money is only used if the goal is reached and, if not, 100% is refunded to each person. The first {exempt} of each year pays no commission.

sections.title: Who it is for
bullets: Cultural associations, music bands, choirs and orchestras.
Theatre and dance groups and music schools.
Foundations and trusts that run activities with their community.

sections.title: What you can do
bullets: Fund instruments, costumes, scenery, tours or premises refurbishments.
Sell QR tickets for concerts and performances, with capacity controlled.
Organise your community into groups you configure: students or members, families, teachers or instructors, friends and supporters, former members.
Decide with a quorum and a double signature which projects go ahead.

sections.title: Transparency with your supporters
paragraphs: Every campaign shows its identified pot, its deadline and how the goal breaks down into four lines that add up exactly to the total. Anyone who contributes knows where their money goes and what happens if the goal is not reached.

sections.title: What it costs
paragraphs: Registration is free. The first {exempt} of each year pays no commission; after that, from {t1Rate} to {t3Rate} depending on the size of the project.

culturales.ctaText: Open your community’s ideas box and launch your first campaign with a 100% refund if the goal is not reached.

comercios.title: Sponsor your neighbourhood school or club
comercios.description: Sponsor your neighbourhood school or club: 100% reaches the initiative, you gain visibility among families and get your receipt straight away.
comercios.h1: How to sponsor your neighbourhood school or club
comercios.answer: A business sponsors an initiative by choosing a level of €100, €250 or €500. 100% of that amount reaches the initiative in full; the advertising management fee ({sponsorFee} plus VAT) is added on top and paid by the business, which receives the sponsorship receipt and the fee invoice straight away.

sections.title: What your business gets
bullets: A place as a friendly business on the organisation’s page, in the Gold, Silver or Bronze category, with no amounts shown publicly.
Visibility among neighbourhood families throughout the school year.
Your own offer or coupon for families, if you want to give one.
A sponsorship receipt and the invoice for the management fee, by email straight away.

steps.title: Find your neighbourhood organisation
steps.text: Look up the school, club or cultural organisation you want to support.

steps.title: Choose a level
steps.text: Pick €100, €250 or €500 and pay by card or Bizum.

steps.title: Receive your receipt and invoice
steps.text: The sponsorship receipt and the fee invoice reach you by email straight away, with no paperwork.

steps.title: Appear as a friendly business
steps.text: Your business is shown in its category during the school year.

sections.title: If the campaign does not reach its goal
paragraphs: The sponsorship is reassigned according to the organisation’s rule. If there is no other active campaign, it is kept as a credit pot in the business’s name for a limited period and, if unused, refunded to it.

comercios.ctaText: Find the school or club you want to sponsor and get started in minutes.

comoFunciona.title: How the platform works
comoFunciona.description: From idea to improvement in 4 steps: ideas with a quorum, double signature, all-or-nothing contributions via Paycomet and a 100% refund if not reached.
comoFunciona.h1: How KORUM works, step by step
comoFunciona.answer: On KORUM a community proposes an improvement, backs it with signatures, two people from the organisation approve it and families fund it with all-or-nothing contributions: the money is collected through Paycomet and, if the goal is not reached in time, 100% is refunded to each person.

steps.title: Propose and gather signatures
steps.text: A family proposes an idea under a private alias. Others back it with their signature until the quorum is reached.

steps.title: Double signature by the organisation
steps.text: Two different people from the organisation approve the idea. The organisation freely chooses its supplier and the platform works out the goal.

steps.title: Families contribute in 10 seconds
steps.text: With Bizum or card and just their email. Every initiative has its own identified pot and a deadline.

steps.title: Enjoy the Before and After
steps.text: When the goal is reached, the improvement is paid for with the supplier’s invoice in hand and the result is published.

sections.title: What happens to the money
paragraphs: Payments are processed by Paycomet and the money is held until the goal is reached. KORUM records it in a double-entry ledger, to the cent. If the last contribution takes the total above the goal, the surplus goes in full to the organisation as an additional project reserve.

sections.title: And if the goal is not reached
paragraphs: A campaign lasts at most {maxDays} days. If it does not reach 100% in that time and the organisation does not decide to resize it, Paycomet automatically refunds 100% of what was collected to each person, voluntary contribution included, to the original payment method.

sections.title: Who is involved
bullets: Families and members propose, sign and contribute.
The organisation approves with a double signature, chooses its supplier and receives the money.
Neighbourhood businesses sponsor and gain visibility.
Paycomet carries out the payments, the holding of funds and the refunds.
KORUM provides the technology and does not hold the money.

comoFunciona.ctaTitle: Is your community ready to start?
comoFunciona.ctaText: Registration is free and takes a few minutes.

precios.title: Pricing and rates
precios.description: Free registration. The first {exempt} of each school year with no commission; after that, from {t1Rate} to {t3Rate}. See every rate in detail.
precios.h1: KORUM pricing: what is paid and who pays it
precios.answer: Registering an organisation is free. KORUM charges a banded commission only on the part above the first {exempt} of each school year, and the cost of the payment gateway is already included in the goal families see.

sections.title: What the goal families see includes
paragraphs: The public page of each initiative splits the goal into four lines that add up exactly to the total:
bullets: Supplier quote and equipment.
Installation and technical set-up.
Maintenance, risk and contingency reserve.
Payment gateway, platform, management and refund guarantee.

sections.title: Who pays what
bullets: The organisation pays nothing to register.
Families contribute to the goal and, if they wish, a voluntary contribution to KORUM that arrives unticked.
Businesses pay the sponsorship level, which arrives in full, plus the advertising management fee.
Whoever buys a ticket or a raffle ticket pays the “digital management fees”, always in plain sight.

sections.title: The voluntary contribution to KORUM
paragraphs: It is optional and changes nothing about the donation. It supports the service that guarantees every family that 100% of their donation reaches the school, an automatic refund if the goal is not reached, and the automatic issue of their certificate or receipt.

precios.ctaText: Register your organisation for free and the Studio will calculate the exact goal from your quote.

seguridad.title: Security and transparency
seguridad.description: Who handles the money, how spending is approved, what happens if the goal is not reached and how your data is protected on KORUM.
seguridad.h1: Security and transparency: who handles the money and the data
seguridad.answer: Payments are processed by PAYCOMET, a payment institution authorised by the Bank of Spain. KORUM is the technology: it never holds your money. Every initiative has its own identified pot, and the money is held at Paycomet until the goal is reached.

sections.title: What KORUM is and is not
paragraphs: KORUM is a technology platform: it is not a financial institution and does not hold funds. Payments, the holding of funds, transfers and refunds are carried out by Paycomet.
KORUM never intermediates or approves suppliers of works or equipment and never charges them commissions: each organisation chooses freely.

sections.title: How spending is approved
paragraphs: Approving an idea and releasing funds requires the signatures of two different people from the organisation, both with two-step verification. Payment is made with the supplier’s invoice in hand and recorded in a ledger that cannot be edited: mistakes are corrected with a reversing entry.

sections.title: If the goal is not reached
paragraphs: 100% of what was collected is refunded to each person, to the original payment method and automatically.

sections.title: Your data
bullets: No tracking cookies or third-party pixels: visit analytics do not use cookies.
The tax ID provided for the tax certificate is stored encrypted.
Families’ ideas and the payment process are not indexed by search engines.
Before and After photos are only published if the organisation confirms that no recognisable minors appear.
You can ask for a copy or the deletion of your data at any time.

seguridad.ctaText: Register your organisation and check every step in your dashboard.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Clear answers on money, refunds, double signatures, commissions, raffles, tax certificates and personal data on KORUM.
faq.answer: Here we answer, in plain language, what organisations, families and businesses ask us most.

faq.a: Paycomet, a payment institution authorised by the Bank of Spain, processes payments and holds the money until the goal is reached. KORUM is the technology and does not hold your money.

faq.q: What happens if the goal is not reached?
faq.a: 100% of what was collected is refunded to each person, to the original payment method and automatically, including the voluntary contribution to KORUM.

faq.q: What happens if the goal is exceeded?
faq.a: The initiative is marked as achieved, closes to new contributions and the surplus goes in full to the organisation as an additional project reserve.

faq.q: How long does a campaign last?
faq.a: At most {maxDays} days from publication, because Paycomet only allows funds to be split within a limited period after each payment.
Registration is free. The first {exempt} of each school year pays no commission; after that, from {t1Rate} to {t3Rate} depending on the size of the initiative. Full rates are on the pricing page.
Yes, always through its parents’ association, which is the organisation that owns the funds. Subsidised and private schools do so through their owner.

faq.q: Can we choose our own supplier?
faq.a: Yes, always. KORUM never intermediates or approves suppliers of works or equipment and never charges them commissions.
Two different people: the main manager (head teacher, club chair…) and a co-signer (chair of the parents’ association, club treasurer…). Both are needed to approve an idea and to release funds.

Yes, with numbered tickets and a certified on-screen draw. Raffles are regulated by each autonomous community and may require prior notification or authorisation: the organisation confirms it complies with its own rules before publishing.

faq.q: Do I need to sign up to contribute?
faq.a: No. To contribute or buy tickets, your email is enough, and that is where your receipt or tickets arrive instantly. To propose or sign ideas you do need a verified account.

faq.q: Will I receive a tax certificate?
faq.a: Only if the organisation has its Law 49/2002 status accredited. Otherwise you receive a named contribution receipt.

faq.q: What does a sponsoring business receive?
faq.a: It appears as a friendly business in its category (Gold, Silver or Bronze), receives the sponsorship receipt and the fee invoice straight away, and 100% of the chosen level reaches the initiative.
We do not use tracking cookies, the tax ID is stored encrypted, and you can ask for a copy or the deletion of your data whenever you like.
